description:
FactSlot (facts.rs ~183) keys publishers, dirty_publishers and unfinal_publishers by bare Job; DependencyIndex holds one read set, one wait set and one output set per job; read_finality is per publisher. So every fact a job publishes in one run shares the job's read set and the job's clean-or-dirty verdict. The scope walk (jobs/source.rs scope_code, and DefineModule for module surfaces) publishes one FunctionSource(f) per function from one job, so each function's fact inherits (layer 1) the walk's dirtiness while it waits on an item-macro expansion and (layer 2) the walk's read on that expansion product even for functions defined above the macro. Reproducer (five lines):
  defmacro define_answer() do
    {:def, %{}, [{:answer, %{}, []}, [{:do, 9}]]}
  end
  define_answer()
  def main(), do: answer()
The macro's own source FunctionId(36) is claimed by the blocked walk, and defining 36 needs it: FunctionDefined(36) <- DefineFunction <- ExpandedFunctionSource(36) <- ExpandFunctionSource <- FunctionSource(36) <- ScopeCode(17)[blocked on Product root 3]. After the expansion the concluded walk's read set includes Product(root 3), so RootEntry(3)'s ground reaches the product being driven. Under the strict drain rule (fz-kdt.227) 11 lib tests stall with "backend product for root N waited on Settled(RootEntry(RootId(N))) with no ready producer" (list in fz-kdt.226's history: compiler2_test def_and_defp_bounce..., body_test quote_preserves..., macro_product_test source_less..., port_macros_test x2, port_misc_test x3, product_drive_test standalone_drive_owns..., source_publish_test x2). Fixing either layer alone leaves all 11 red; fixing both turns the 82-test selection green (measured with probes).

Rejected: segments. In ordinary fz every def is a macro call (00181: Enum.fz 147 forms, 147 macro calls, 0 functions), so "one segment per item macro" is one job per definition (~199 jobs on a 443-job fixture); a syntactic cut at non-definition macro calls needs a boundary-state store keyed by (owner, segment) carrying namespace, current module, local callables, pending types, required remote macros, the module interface, revision floor and struct flag, the stash tier one level up, plus the same for DefineModule. Chosen by the user 2026-09-16: derivation identity ("more from less").

Design: a job run may conclude several derivations. A derivation has its own reads, outputs and changed set and concludes when it is returned; the run's waits belong to the job's own final derivation. Publisher identity becomes (Job, derivation) wherever the scheduler keys on publisher: FactSlot sets, DependencyIndex reads/outputs, read_finality, rebased, output-key retraction in the work graph. Most jobs conclude exactly one derivation, so their shape is unchanged. The scope walk concludes one derivation per function at the point it scopes it, with exactly the reads accumulated so far (source_publish.rs accumulates reads and product_reads in source order, so the prefix at each define_source_function is that function's ground), and its final derivation carries CodeScoped/ModuleDefined with the whole read set and any wait. Then the macro's source is clean and grounded above the macro, both layers vanish by construction, and a real self-cycle through a macro's product is still refused. Research first and report before building: size the mechanical change (every publisher-keyed site); whether the existing cumulative contribution discipline (activation_input_contributions, accumulate-on-extend / replace-on-conclude) is the same idea and can be folded into derivations rather than kept beside them; what retraction of a superseded derivation means when a re-scope drops a function; telemetry shape (completion records name the derivation). Failing-first: a generic scheduler test where one job run concludes a derivation while its final derivation waits, and the concluded claim is certified under the strict drain rule; then the 11 tests above green with the fz-kdt.227 patch applied. Concept count: derivations replace the per-job read/wait/output shape, they do not sit beside it; list removed and added by name. Pins may only move down; corpus canon byte-identical. Docs: fact-engine.md ownership section as present-tense facts.
title: The scheduler owns claims per job; a job that publishes several facts in one run must be able to conclude each on its own reads (derivation identity)
